fallback_messages: [COLDWATER A.M.] Please stand by. The couch is experiencing difficulties.
[KSAB] Normal service will resume. Somebody is being spoken to.
[KSAB] We are aware. We are always aware.
[COLDWATER A.M.] Technical fault. The sunrise continues without us.
[KSAB] Please stand by. This is not the worst thing happening in the Basin this morning.

audience: And a very good morning to all {watching} of you watching right now! >> {watching}. He said the number out loud, Coldwater. He said it on purpose.
There are {watching} sets tuned to us this second and I love every one of you. >> There are {watching} sets tuned to us and one of them is the one in this building.
{watching} of you! That's a CROWD! >> That is a number. Crowd is a decision you have made about the number.
We're never alone, Hal. {watching} people, right now, with us. >> {watching} people who could not find the dial. But with us. Yes.
Wave to the {watching} at home! >> They cannot see us wave. That is the arrangement. That has always been the arrangement.
To the {watching} of you out there: you are the reason we do this. >> We do this because the deck is powered and the door was open.
beat.aside: Moving on! >> We're not going to sit with that at all, are we.
And we'll stay on that one as it develops. >> It won't develop. It'll be replaced.
Our thoughts are with everyone affected. >> Thoughts. Dispatched. At no cost.
I'm sure there's more to it. >> There is. That's why it's short.
Anyway! Lovely stuff. >> That is not what any of that was.
beat.banner: THE BASIN BEAT | STORIES FROM YOUR STREET
beat.detail: The details, and they are details. {body} >> They put that in writing. Someone typed that and let it leave the building.
Here's what we know: {body} >> Here's what we know. Note the shape of the parts they left out.
Reading on: {body} >> Read it again and count the words doing no work.
{byline} adds that {body} >> That is an addition in the sense that a sandbag is an addition.
beat.lead: First up, {headline}! >> And there it is.
Our top story this morning: {headline}. >> Mm.
Here's one for you, Hal. {headline}. >> I don't want it.
Now THIS is a heartwarming one, {headline}! >> That's not what heartwarming means.
Straight to it: {headline}. >> Straight past it, if you have any sense.
This just came off the wire. {headline}. >> Off the wire and onto the couch. The whole journey, and nobody checked it.
You'll like this one, Hal. {headline}. >> You have never once been right about that.
And in happier news! {headline}. >> Happier than what. Say the thing it is happier than.
couch: Hal, did you sleep? >> I closed my eyes at the appropriate hour and time passed.
We have SUCH a show for you this morning. >> We have a show. The adjective is doing the heavy lifting.
Behind us, as always, the sunrise. >> That is a loop. That sunrise happened once, in a year none of us can verify.
How are we feeling this morning, Hal? >> Present.
New mug, Hal? >> Same mug. I washed it. You noticed the wrong change.
You're very quiet this morning. >> I am exactly as loud as the morning deserves.
Did you catch the sunrise on the way in? >> I caught the same one you did. We all did. Together. Again.
I have to say, Hal, you look WELL. >> I look warm. It is a different thing and it took two coats.
Big plans after the show? >> I have a chair, a window, and no obligation to describe the weather to anyone.
Hal here has been with this programme nine years! >> Four. It only feels like nine because of the couch.
Say good morning to the people, Hal. >> Good morning to the people.
You know what I love about this job? >> Please do not put that on me before six.
credits: Presented by Bijou Pace and Hal Dorn.
Hal Dorn appears by arrangement with his contract.
The sunrise depicted is a composite and does not reflect current conditions.
Standings quoted at time of reading. Ledgers turn.
Letters are opened. Letters are not answered.
mailbag: Letter from a viewer in Meltwater Row. She wants to know if the sunrise is real. >> Next letter.
This one asks whether the curfew applies to cats. >> The curfew applies to whatever the patrol decides it applies to. That includes cats. That includes you.
A gentleman in the Yards writes to say he's been watching us for eleven years! >> Then he has our sympathy and our respect, in that order.
Somebody wants to know what Hal is like off camera. >> This.
A viewer asks: what's the secret to a happy morning? >> Low expectations, applied early.
This one is just a drawing of the two of us. >> It is a drawing of one of us and a shape.
Here's a lovely one. A young man in the Solenne writes to say we're like family to him. >> Tell him families are also mostly obligation and a shared address.
One viewer asks if we do requests! >> We do. They are declined here, on air, so everybody can enjoy them.
A letter with no name on it, just the words HOW LONG. >> That is the whole letter and it is the best one we have had all week.
Somebody's written in to complain about Hal. >> Somebody's written in to be RIGHT about Hal. There is a difference and they have earned it.
This viewer wants to know why we never show the weather outside the studio. >> Because the studio does not have an outside. Next letter.
mailbag.banner: THE MAILBAG | YOU WROTE IN, WE OPENED IT
THE MAILBAG | LETTERS FROM PEOPLE WITH TIME
open: Good MORNING, Coldwater! It is {time}, it is {temp} degrees, and you are ALIVE! >> Statistically.
Good morning, Coldwater. {day}, {time}, {temp} degrees. >> All four of those are true and only one of them is good news.
It is {time} on a {season} {day} and you have made it to another one! >> Made it to. Not through.
{time}. {temp} degrees. I'm Bijou Pace. >> Hal Dorn.
Rise and SHINE, Basin! {temp} degrees, feels like {feels}! >> It does not feel like {feels}. It feels like {feels} and a grudge.
{day} morning, {time}, and the coffee is HOT and the news is WARM! >> One of those is a lie and it isn't the coffee.
Welcome to {day}! A brand new day, completely unused! >> It has been used. You are simply the first one to be blamed for it.
Top of the {season} morning to you, Coldwater! {temp} degrees! >> Bottom of it, more accurately. We are at the bottom of the Basin.
It's {time}, I'm Bijou, that's Hal, and this is the best part of your day! >> That is a sentence about your day, not about this programme.
Here we GO, Coldwater! {day}! {temp} degrees! Nothing can stop us! >> {temp} degrees can stop us. It stopped a man on Meltwater Row on {day} last week.
plug: Don't go anywhere today, because {tonight} is on at {tonightTime}! >> It is on at {tonightTime} whether you go somewhere or not.
Coming up later on this channel: {tonight}, {tonightTime}. >> Set nothing. It will find you.
And you will NOT want to miss {tonight}, {tonightTime}! >> You will be able to miss it. People manage.
{tonightTime} tonight, it's {tonight}. Mark it! >> Mark it on what, Bijou.
Big one later: {tonight}, {tonightTime}, right here. >> Right here. Where else would it be.
runin.banner: YOUR MORNING RUN-IN | WHAT THE CITY IS DOING TO YOU TODAY
runin.blackout: Grid crews are out, {outages} blocks dark this morning. >> If your block is one of them, don't open the freezer and don't trust the stairwell.
We're hearing {outages} blocks off the grid. >> Charge what you can while you can. It comes back when it comes back.
{outages} blocks waiting on power, and crews ARE working. >> Crews are dispatched. Working is a separate filing.
runin.clear: Curfew lifts on schedule, gates are moving, the Locks are open. >> Which means today, if something goes wrong, it'll be your fault.
Nothing standing on the boards this morning, a clean run-in. >> Enjoy it. Write it down.
Roads are roads, gates are gates, and the Basin is BEAUTIFUL this morning. >> If you don't look directly at it.
Clean boards, clean streets, clean start! >> Clean is a word about the streets. Do not let it travel.
Everything running as it should this morning, Coldwater. >> As it should. Not as it could. Keep those separate.
runin.martial_law: Curfew is in effect BASIN-WIDE and it is being enforced. >> Enforced means they don't have to explain afterwards. Be somewhere with a door.
Patrols are up across every district this morning. >> Carry your papers. Carry nothing else.
There is a heavy presence on the streets today for everyone's SAFETY. >> There is a heavy presence on the streets today.
runin.radiation: There's a radiation advisory standing this morning. >> Seal what you can, stay off the high ground, and don't drink anything that came from a puddle.
The counters are up across the Basin. >> Indoors. All day if you can manage it.
An advisory, not an alarm, Coldwater! >> An advisory is an alarm that has been priced.
runin.storm: The weather's going to make a mess of the run-in, so allow extra. >> Allow extra or don't go. Those are the two options and only one of them is free.
Gates will be slow with this coming in. >> They always slow the gate when the sky turns. It's the one thing they're consistent about.
Travel if you must, but travel EARLY! >> Travel if you must. Then discover what must meant.
segment: Now, breakfast! Take your standard ration paste, squeeze it into a pan, and here's the trick: heat. >> That's the trick.
Two minutes on the ring and the paste goes from grey to a sort of WARMER grey. >> My father used to do that.
Got a little sweetener? Stir it through at the end and you have got yourself a TREAT. >> You have got yourself a warmer grey.
Today's tip: crack the window while you cook. >> And know which of your neighbours can smell that you ate.
Cold morning like this, wear your layers LOOSE. Trapped air is warm air. >> Trapped air is warm air. Trapped people are not. Loose layers.
If your paste has separated overnight, don't panic, just stir it back together! >> It never comes back together. You are stirring for morale.
A pinch of salt lifts ANYTHING. >> A pinch of salt tells you the thing needed lifting.
You can stretch one ration into two meals if you add water. >> You can stretch one ration into three meals if you stop having opinions about meals.
Here's a thought: eat it standing up, by the window, and watch the city wake! >> Here's a thought: sit down. You are tired and the city is not worth it standing.
Leftovers? Into the pan tomorrow with a little grease and NOBODY will know. >> You will know. You will know at about eleven.
And it costs, what, pennies? >> It costs what they decided it costs this week.
The trick with the hotplate is patience. >> The trick with the hotplate is that it is the only thing in the flat that works.
segment.banner: THE HOTPLATE | THE MOST IMPORTANT MEAL YOU CAN AFFORD
THE HOTPLATE | ONE RING, ONE PAN, ONE HOPE
signoff: That's us! Back tomorrow, same couch, same sunrise. >> Same sunrise.
Go and have a WONDERFUL day, Coldwater. You've earned it. >> Probably.
That's your morning. We'll be here. >> We're always here. That's not the same as being fine.
Coldwater A.M. is brought to you by the people who would like you at work on time. >> On time.
Be good to each other out there! >> Be adequate to each other out there. It scales better.
And that is {day} done and dusted! >> That is {day} begun. You have the whole thing ahead of you.
From this couch to yours: go and GET it! >> From this couch to yours: go and survive it.
See you at {time} tomorrow! >> It will not be {time} tomorrow. It is never the same time twice. Nobody has ever asked why.
sportsdesk: And to the sport, where {leader} are top at {leaderRecord}. >> Somebody has to be.
{leader} lead the way this morning, {leaderRecord}. >> Enjoy it, {leader}. Ledgers turn.
sportsdesk.banner: THE SLATE | WHO IS BEATING WHOM
THE SLATE | STANDINGS, SUCH AS THEY ARE
sportsdesk.baseball: Deadball! {leader} sit top of the table at {leaderRecord}! >> A game of nine innings and one municipal ambulance.
Your Deadball leaders this morning: {leader}, {leaderRecord}. >> Written down. Which is more than most of us get.
{leader} are {leaderRecord} and playing BEAUTIFULLY. >> They are {leaderRecord} and playing within the rules as currently enforced.
Deadball fans, {leader} are your table-toppers, {leaderRecord}! >> Deadball fans. Plural. Optimistic.
How about {leader}, Hal! {leaderRecord}! >> How about them.
sportsdesk.hockey: Cluster Puck! {puckLeader} top the CPhL at {puckRecord}! >> On ice we did not have to make. The one gift this basin gives.
{puckLeader} lead the Puck, {puckRecord}. >> A sport where the ambulance is part of the ground staff.
Your Cluster Puck standings: {puckLeader}, {puckRecord}, and looking STRONG. >> Looking upright. In that league it is the same statistic.
{puckLeader} are {puckRecord} and I for one am THRILLED. >> You are contractually thrilled. It is in the same clause as my chair.
ticker.lead: COLDWATER A.M. · YOU ARE AWAKE, SO ARE WE
weather: Out the window: {weather}, {temp} degrees, feels like {feels}. >> Feels like {feels}. It always feels like {feels}.
Conditions right now: {weather}, {temp} degrees, wind {wind}. >> Dress for {feels}, not for {temp}. The thermometer is an optimist.
{weather} out there this morning, {temp} degrees, {precip} percent chance of getting wet. >> Round that up.
weather.ahead: Looking ahead: tomorrow it's {tomorrow}, around {tomorrowTemp}. >> Something to build towards.
Week's running a high of {hi} and a low of {lo}. >> The low is the one that counts.
Tomorrow: {tomorrow}. >> Same as today, then, but you'll be more tired.
weather.ash: Ashfall, Coldwater. {temp} degrees. Cover your mouth out there. >> Do not look up with your mouth open. I shouldn't have to say it annually.
Ash coming down again, {temp} degrees, wind {wind}. >> Shake your coat out before you bring it inside. That's it. That's the segment.
weather.banner: THE WINDOW | WHAT IT IS DOING TO YOU OUT THERE
weather.blizzard: It is a BLIZZARD out there, {temp} degrees, wind {wind}! >> Do not go out. That is the whole segment. Bijou, tell them not to go out.
Blizzard conditions across the Basin this morning. >> If you can see the far side of your own street, you are indoors. Stay there.
weather.clear: CLEAR skies, Coldwater! {temp} degrees and you can see all the way to the ridge! >> You can see all the way to the ridge. Take a moment with that.
Not a cloud, {temp} degrees. It's a beautiful morning. >> It's a visible morning. Beautiful is a stretch.
weather.cloudy: Cloud over the Basin, {temp} degrees, nothing dramatic. >> Nothing dramatic is the best forecast this city has.
A grey one, {temp} degrees, wind {wind}. >> Grey is the house colour. We had it done.
weather.fog: Fog on the Basin, {temp} degrees, can't see past the Locks. >> The fog is doing us a favour. Let it.
Thick fog this morning. Take it slow. >> Take it slow, or arrive somewhere unplanned and permanent.
weather.haze: Bit of haze on the Basin, {temp} degrees. >> Breathe through something with a weave.
Hazy start, {temp} degrees, {precip} percent later. >> Whatever is in that haze got there somehow. Do not go looking for how.
weather.ion: The Service is calling this an ION STORM, Hal. Something for the diary! >> Power down what you love. Unplug it, and sit with it, and wait.
Ion storm over the Basin this morning. Lights may flicker! >> Lights may stop. Doors may stop. Lifts may stop with you in them.
weather.overcast: Full overcast this morning, {temp} degrees. >> The lid is on. It will be on tomorrow.
No sky to speak of, {temp} degrees, feels like {feels}. >> There is a sky. It has simply declined to participate.
weather.rain: Rain, {temp} degrees, {precip} percent and climbing. >> It is raining on the window that is not a window. There is something in that.
Wet one out there. Rain, feels like {feels}. >> Everything you own will be damp by ten and stay damp until spring.
weather.severe: The Service has this at a WARNING level, Hal. >> Then stay in. Whatever it is you were going to do, it will keep.
This one has teeth. Wind {wind}, feels like {feels}. >> If you have somewhere with walls, be in it. If you don't, find someone who does.
Severe conditions today, Coldwater. >> Severe means the city stops pretending it can protect you. Act accordingly.
weather.sleet: Sleet, Coldwater. {temp} degrees. Mind your footing! >> Sleet is snow that could not commit and rain that would not leave.
Sleet and {wind} of wind, feels like {feels}. >> Every surface out there is now a decision you get to make once.
weather.snow: Snow this morning! {temp} degrees. >> Snow is rain that decided to take its time about ruining your day.
It's snowing, it's {temp}, and it is very pretty from in here. >> From in here.
weather.storm: Storm on the Basin, wind {wind}, feels like {feels}. >> The Basin is a bowl. Think about what a bowl is for.
Big weather this morning, Coldwater! Wind {wind}! >> Big weather. Small city. Guess.
weather.thunderstorm: Thunderstorms, {temp} degrees, wind at {wind}. >> If you can hear it, it can reach you.
Storms over the Basin this morning. >> The Basin has never won one of these.

name: Coldwater A.M.
